title: Robert Louis Stevenson: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde — Ep 01/10 — "Story of the Door"
description:
A lawyer named Utterson and his kinsman Richard Enfield take their Sunday walk through London and stop before a blistered, windowless door. Enfield says he knows an odd story about it, and tells how, on a black winter morning, he saw a small man in a wideawake hat trample calmly over a running child and leave her screaming on the cobbles before that very door.

Enfield collared the man, whose single ugly look brought the sweat out on him. The gathering crowd swore to ruin the man's name, so he bought their silence with gold and a cheque signed at a bank that honored it the next morning -- a house Enfield has called Black Mail House ever since. Enfield will not say more; the more a thing looks like Queer Street, he says, the less he asks.

Utterson presses only for the name, since he says he already knows the other party in the business. Enfield gives it: Hyde. Utterson admits, 'I do not ask the other party's name. I know it already,' and the two shake hands on their bargain of silence as a tramp strikes a match against the door's stained panel behind them -- the door keeping its secret, and Hyde keeping its key.

Chapter STORY OF THE DOOR of Part One of Robert Louis Stevenson's Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, "", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
